H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper distinguishes Manual/Auto mode and an Auto transferring procedure, but presents the controller as a flat SCADA workflow rather than explicit composite parent/child states.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Guards combine interlocks, level change, flow sensing, totalized quantity, valve feedback, pump failure, manual override, and low-level conditions; e.g., running continues only if source level decreases AND line flow is sensed.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Start opens destination/dispensing/suction valves and starts the pump; pause closes all opened valves and stops the pump; completion turns the pump off, closes valves, and updates SCADA displays/animations/status.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: Dedicated pause/recovery exists: any listed deviation during transfer pauses the process, the interlock is corrected or troubleshot, and the user restarts by clicking Start again.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: Core actions are in the Algorithm section, while precheck interlocks, detailed pause deviations, interlock screen behavior, and restart are described later in the Procedure section.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as safety interlock, manual override, pump dry run/tripped/failed, and valve feedback imply control rules beyond simple event names.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Actions are embedded in narrative prose around SCADA screens and figures, not in a co-located state-action table: start, pause, completion, display, and restart behavior must be attributed back to states.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The controller uses multi-variable boolean guards such as level-decreasing AND flow-sensed, no tank-level change AND no line-flow change, and all interlocks satisfied.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No explicit composite state has its own entry/during/exit behavior beyond substates; the mode structure is procedural and mostly flat.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: Fault pause is specified for deviations in the middle of transfer, not as an explicit any-state global transition across multiple substates.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: No deep composite state or non-trivial init/pseudo-state chain is described.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: Several guards involve level/flow deltas, quantity availability, totalized-flow comparison, valve feedback, and interlock combinations, making expression normalization and consistency checking useful.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: No explicit cross-cutting rule applies to three or more substates, and no parent composite state clearly owns a shared during action.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Most actions are concrete pump/valve commands, but SCADA alarm/interlock display/status animation side effects are somewhat abstract supervisory outputs.

key_nl_quotes: If Level in source tank decreases and flow sensor in line senses the liquid/solvent flow then operation remains continues otherwise operation will be paused automatically.
If any one of the following deviation occurs in the middle of the process then the process will be paused.
one_line_pitch: A compact PLC/SCADA transfer supervisor whose behavior depends on quantity totalization, flow/level interlocks, valve feedback, pump faults, pause actions, and operator recovery.
rationale: This is a strong stress-test for guard and action extraction: the paper gives multiple interlocked conditions and multi-actuator side effects that prior Umple-style baselines are weak at recovering. It also has meaningful pause/recovery logic with several fault causes, although the recovery is not an explicit any-state global escape and the hierarchy signal is weak. The baseline-trap density is high because the relevant rules are split across algorithm prose, SCADA procedure text, and domain terms such as interlock and override.
